body.p: Author/editor/indexer relationshipsabout To paraphrase Casablanca, every index is potentially the beginning of a beautiful relationship. It may be a simple, businesslike, two-person dialogue between an editor and an indexer; it may be a sweeping soap opera involving a cast of lead editor, production editor, compositor, subject indexer, names indexer, author, and the author’s secretary and graduate students.

section.title: The Importance of Communication
section.p: Author/editor/indexer relationshipscommunication, importance of Communicationimportance of Good communication between all parties is essential for a successful indexing project. The editor should establish clear expectations early and maintain open channels throughout the process.

section.title: Authors and Indexes
section.p: AuthorsAuthor/editor/indexer relationships Author/editor/indexer relationshipsauthors and indexes Author/editor/indexer relationshipsauthors, common queries from Author/editor/indexer relationshipsauthor term lists Authors have a deep understanding of their own work and can provide valuable input to the indexer. Author term lists—lists of key terms that the author considers important—can be very helpful. However, authors sometimes have difficulty seeing their work from the reader’s perspective, which is essential for good indexing.

section.title: Editors and Indexes
section.p: Author/editor/indexer relationshipseditors and indexes Author/editor/indexer relationshipseditorial responsibility Editors typically serve as the intermediary between author and indexer. The editor is responsible for ensuring that the index meets the publisher’s standards and serves the intended audience.

section.title: Indexers and Indexes
section.p: Author/editor/indexer relationshipsindexers and indexes Professional indexers bring specialized skills to the project, including the ability to identify concepts, select appropriate terminology, and create a structure that serves users.

section.title: Schedules and Payment
section.p: Author/editor/indexer relationshipsschedules Author/editor/indexer relationshipspayment Author/editor/indexer relationshipscontracts Author/editor/indexer relationshipssubcontracting by indexer Realistic scheduling is critical. The indexer needs adequate time to produce a quality index, and the editor needs to factor in time for review and revisions. Payment terms and contracts should be agreed upon before work begins.

section.title: Text Transmission and Changes
section.p: Author/editor/indexer relationshipstext, transmission to indexer Author/editor/indexer relationshipstext changes Author/editor/indexer relationshipschanges, prompt notification of The method of transmitting text to the indexer (electronic files, proofs, etc.) and handling changes during the indexing process should be agreed upon in advance. Prompt notification of changes is essential to avoid rework.

section.title: Index Revisions
section.p: Author/editor/indexer relationshipsindex revisions Author/editor/indexer relationshipsindex previews Author/editor/indexer relationshipsqueries from indexer Communicationduring indexing process Revisions may be needed after the editor reviews the index. A preview of the index partway through the project can catch problems early. Indexer queries during the process are a sign of careful work and should be answered promptly.
